title: Recipe
description: Hearty shredded root vegetable 'nests' form a crispy guard for a savory, dune-colored lentil filling. A super dish for a cold winter day, finished with a surprising kick of crystalized ginger.
name: Crystal-Guarded Winter Dune Nests

wet.name: Full-fat coconut cream
wet.notes: chilled, from the top of a can of coconut milk

instructions.description: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Grease a 6-cup standard muffin tin.

In a large bowl, combine the shredded sweet potatoes and parsnips. Squeeze out as much moisture as possible using a clean kitchen towel. Return to the bowl and toss with cornstarch, 2 Tbs of olive oil, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.

Divide the vegetable mixture among 4-6 cups of the muffin tin, pressing firmly into the bottom and up the sides to form 'nest' shapes. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and crispy. This is your 'guard'.

While the nests bake, prepare the 'dune' filling. Heat the remaining 1 Tbs of olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Sauté the onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

Stir in the red lentils, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and smoked paprika. Add the vegetable broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the lentils are very soft and have absorbed most of the liquid.

Remove from heat and stir in the lemon juice and nutritional yeast. Season with salt and pepper to taste. You can lightly mash the mixture with a fork for a more rustic texture or use an immersion blender for a smoother purée.

Once the nests are baked, let them cool in the tin for a few minutes before carefully removing them. Fill each nest with the warm lentil mixture. Top with a dollop of chilled coconut cream and a generous sprinkle of the 'crystal' chopped ginger before serving.

notes: The rustic, slightly messy look of the nests is part of the 'disastaspect' charm! This recipe is naturally gluten-free. For a different flavor profile, try using carrots or celeriac in the nests.
